title: Synthetic minority oversampling technique for multiclass imbalance problems
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: no (Table 1, p. 334: all 27 sets keep L >= 3; some original labels are merged into 3+ groups, e.g. automobile '1'&'2'/'3'&'4'&'5'/'6', vowel5, pendigits, machine, ESL; one-vs-rest class transformation is used only for the baselines ADASYN, SL-SMOTE and MWMOTE, Sec. 4.1, p. 335)
link (Core / Partial / Not counted): Core (Alg. 1 step 8.2, p. 330: the only generator is Eq. (1), si = xi + (xj - xi).*gamma, interpolation between a class-c seed and a class-c neighbour; Eq. (1) given on p. 328)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): n (Alg. 1 steps 7-8, p. 330: every xi in S^c is a seed; Sec. 3.3, p. 334: same number of synthetic points per instance; the NBDOS split into outstanding/trapped instances, Sec. 3.1, pp. 330-331, only changes how the partner is drawn)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): n (Alg. 1 step 7, p. 330: zeta spread over all members of S^c as evenly as possible; Sec. 3.3, p. 334: equal number per minority instance; per-class zeta = gap to the largest class, Sec. 4.1, p. 335)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): y (Alg. 1 steps 5, 6, 8.1, p. 330; Sec. 3.2, pp. 332-334: for trapped instances the partner is drawn from the k1 = 12 nearest same-class neighbours by weighted sampling, weights from Eq. (2), p. 332, built from the counts and entropy of other minority and majority classes inside the PN hypersphere centred at the midpoint of xi and xj; outstanding instances draw uniformly as in SMOTE; if no PN neighbourhood is pure class c, xi itself is added as a partner with weight 1 + w1/e, step 6.1, p. 330, pp. 333-334; k1 = 12 not 5 and standardized Euclidean distance, Sec. 4.1, p. 335)
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): n (Alg. 1 step 8.2, p. 330 reuses Eq. (1) exactly as the paper states it for SMOTE, p. 328; FLAG: gamma is a random vector with element-wise product, so points fall in the box spanned by xi and xj, p. 332 says the generalization region is a hyper-rectangle, not on the segment; this is the paper's own SMOTE formula, not an SMOM change)
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): n (Alg. 1, p. 330: SI is returned with no cleaning or removal step; over-generalization is handled before generation by the selection weights, Sec. 3.2, p. 332)
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n (Sec. 4.1, p. 335: data are oversampled once as preprocessing, then C4.5, AdaBoost.M1(C4.5), MLP and NB from weka are trained on the result; SMOM is not run inside boosting rounds or training)
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: n (Alg. 1, p. 330 outputs only new synthetic instances SI; no original is deleted or shifted; NBDOS 'drops' small clusters only by resetting their cluster labels to 0 = trapped, Alg. 2 lines 21-25, p. 331; possible outliers are kept and may get copies of themselves via step 6.1, p. 330, pp. 333-334)
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n (Sec. 4.1, p. 335: k1 = 12 and k2 = 8 set by hand, tuning guidance only in the supplement; Exp. 2, p. 337: k reset to class size minus 1 for classes with fewer than 12 instances, for all compared algorithms; a cap, not an adaptive choice)
notes: Judgement quotes: M -> 'All classes are oversampled until they contain as many instances as the largest one.' (p. 335). Neighbour choice -> 'a neighbor instance x^j is selected from x^i.N^c_k1 in the weighted sampling way' (Alg. 1 step 8.1, p. 330); self-partner -> 'add it into its own neighbors set' (p. 333). Allocation -> 'our SMOM generates an equal number of synthetic samples for each minority instance' (p. 334). Placement flag -> 'gamma is a vector in which each element is a random number from [0, 1]' (p. 328) and 'the generalization region is hyperrectangle' (p. 332): coded n because SMOM uses the paper's own SMOTE Eq. (1) unchanged; under the strict scalar-lambda reference it would be y. Multiclass handling: one class at a time, every non-largest class oversampled to the largest class size (p. 335); weights use the whole multiclass data, other classes split into minority/majority at size M/L (p. 334), majority classes down-weighted by w2 = 1/2 (pp. 332, 335); no OVO/OVA for SMOM; class order not stated; whether synthetic points of classes done earlier are part of D for later classes not stated. Other flags: Table 1 label lists do not match L for page-blocks and wine-red (5 labels, L = 4) and housing10 (9 labels, L = 10), p. 334, does not affect M; per-data-set results are only in supplementary Tables S3-S10 (p. 335), not in the article; SMOM handles continuous attributes only (p. 338).
